title: CyclicBarrier vs CountDownLatch: reusable sync-point vs one-time event count
keyPoints: CountDownLatch(N) is a one-time gate: N events count down and waiters unblock when count reaches zero.
CyclicBarrier(N) is a reusable sync point: N threads all call await(), all blocked until the Nth arrives, then all proceed.
CountDownLatch: counting threads and waiting threads can be different. CyclicBarrier: same threads that wait are counted.
CountDownLatch cannot be reset once triggered. CyclicBarrier auto-resets after each trip for multiple phases.
CyclicBarrier accepts an optional barrier action (Runnable) that executes when all threads arrive.
Use latch for 'wait for N events'; use barrier for 'N threads synchronize at checkpoints between phases'.

s1_definition.oneliner: CountDownLatch is a one-time gate where N events count down and waiters unblock at zero, while CyclicBarrier is a reusable sync point where N threads all wait for each other before proceeding together.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **CountDownLatch(N)** – a one-time gate; any thread calls `countDown()` to decrement, any thread calls `await()` to block until count reaches zero; cannot be reset.
- **CyclicBarrier(N)** – a reusable sync point; the same N threads call `await()`, all blocked until the Nth arrives, then all proceed simultaneously; auto-resets after each trip.
- **Counting vs waiting** – in a latch, counting and waiting threads can be different; in a barrier, the same threads do both.
- **Barrier action** – CyclicBarrier accepts an optional Runnable that executes when all threads arrive.
- **Broken state** – if a barrier thread is interrupted or times out, all other waiting threads get `BrokenBarrierException`.
s1_definition.analogy: At National Bank of India: CountDownLatch(3) is the branch manager waiting for 3 department reports. Accounting submits and counts down. Loans submits and counts down. Compliance submits and counts down. Manager proceeds when count reaches zero. Cannot reuse: need a new latch tomorrow. CyclicBarrier(3) is 3 audit teams reaching checkpoint-1 together, then all proceeding to checkpoint-2, then reaching it together again. Same teams, multiple checkpoints, barrier auto-resets.

sections.s3_flow:
```text
  CountDownLatch(3)              CyclicBarrier(3)

  Thread-A: countDown() 3→2      Thread-A: await() ──┐
  Thread-B: countDown() 2→1      Thread-B: await() ──┤ all blocked
  Thread-C: countDown() 1→0      Thread-C: await() ──┘ 3rd arrives!
       │                              │
       ▼                              ▼
  Main: await() unblocks         All 3 released simultaneously
  (count = 0, one-time)          (barrier resets for next trip)

  Latch: different counters/waiters
  Barrier: same threads count and wait
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
CountDownLatch and CyclicBarrier are both synchronizers, but they solve different problems. CountDownLatch(N) is a one-time gate: N events count down, waiters unblock when the count reaches zero, and it cannot be reset. The counting threads and waiting threads can be different. Use it for "wait for N things to happen."

CyclicBarrier(N) is a reusable sync point: N threads all call await(), all are blocked until the Nth arrives, then all proceed simultaneously. It auto-resets after each trip for multiple phases. The same threads that wait are the ones being counted. Use it for "N threads synchronize at checkpoints between phases."

At National Bank of India, the EOD batch uses CyclicBarrier(10) for 10 threads processing three phases: interest calculation, statement generation, and notification sending. All threads must complete each phase before any can start the next. CountDownLatch(4) coordinates the final archive step, waiting for four department batches to complete.

Remember one sentence: latch counts down events one-time, barrier synchronizes the same threads at reusable checkpoints.
